Concrete FAIL findings:

F1 [P1] Wrong plugin discovery root and validation order. Plan lines 223, 229, 238-239 run SyncAgentPlugins from .worktrees/session-lifecycle without AgentPluginParent. Build.SyncAgentPlugins.cs:144-162 defaults discovery to the checkout's immediate parent, which here is F:\GitHub\McpServer\.worktrees, not F:\GitHub. Lines 49-53 permit staged-only success when no sibling repositories are found. ValidatePluginPowerShellOnly runs before synchronization and can validate zero roots or old output (lines 75-86). Repair: pin -AgentPluginParent F:\GitHub (or an explicitly inventoried isolated plugin root), assert the complete expected plugin set was found, perform synchronization once, then validate the generated packages and hashes.

F2 [P1] The named synchronization target is not source-only or repeatable without version changes. Plan lines 223-225 separate source synchronization from installed-cache activation, and line 239 calls SyncAgentPlugins again. The actual target rewrites manifests to the next minor version and calls RefreshKnownPluginCaches (Build.SyncAgentPlugins.cs:63-71). Thus the written flow either updates no real plugins because of F1, or bumps versions and refreshes installed caches twice, before P7 deployment/closure. Repair: explicitly account for the target's version/cache effects; freeze one plugin version and source hash set, select an isolated test destination or approved activation boundary, eliminate the second mutation, and review/validate exactly the generated packages that will be activated. Do not describe this target as only source synchronization.

F3 [P1] The tested tree may differ from the integrated tree even when develop does not advance. Plan lines 169-170 preserve but exclude unrelated changes, while lines 178 and 229 validate the dirty implementation worktree. Line 268 mandates complete reruns only when develop advances. That allows tests to pass with excluded memory/migration/harness changes, followed by integration of a different tree without equivalent validation. Repair: build a clean candidate from the recorded develop SHA plus only the approved file/hunk set, retain the original dirty worktree, and run all required gates and final review against that exact candidate. Require candidate/deployed identity checks regardless of whether develop advanced.

F4 [P2] New Red-to-Green transitions lack an explicit independent review gate. Plan lines 180, 191-192, 196-201, and 216 place code review after implementation/unit green. P0 reviews requirements, but no step blocks production edits until the new mock-backed tests and intended real-code red evidence have received hostile approval. This conflicts with the loaded hostile-phase-gates.md:15-20 requirement for review after AC-covering red tests and before implementation. Repair: add a reusable per-increment requirements -> mock/real-red review -> implementation -> cumulative-green review gate, with explicit AGREE >=98/98 and durable receipt requirements. Correct already-fulfilled behavior remains proof-only; do not manufacture red.

F5 [P2] The machine-report gate is not executable as written for its main unit/provider commands. Plan lines 178 and 229-246 require machine reports and parsing zero-discovery/skips, but Invoke-Pester has no output configuration, Nuke Test only sets a results directory (Build.Test.cs:24-29), and MigrationIntegrationTests sets neither TRX logging nor a report path (Build.TestDependencies.cs:75-80). Unlike the explicit dotnet test commands and PluginSessionLogIntegration target, those listed commands do not establish which fresh machine files exist to parse. Repair: specify supported report-generation configuration or a reviewed validation wrapper, exact per-project result locations, freshness/source identity checks, and executable aggregation that fails on missing reports, zero discovery, failure, or skips. Apply the same complete unit-project inventory at each implementation-slice exit, including the separately excluded Build.Tests where required, not only at P6.

F6 [P2] BUG-TRIAGE-246 documentation is deferred beyond the metadata implementation slice without an explicit plan amendment. Plan lines 187-192 implement and exit metadata contracts, but the three contract documents are first reconciled at lines 218-220. The original Grok plan explicitly locks those documents into S4 and says they are not a later refresh (original plan:93, 109, 168). Repair: move their proof tests and any necessary contract corrections into P2's metadata slice, or explicitly amend the original gate and justify an equivalent noncontradiction guarantee. If the documents already conform, record proof there without changing them.

Concrete UNKNOWN findings requiring a decision, not future execution evidence:

U1 [P1] Import recovery lacks an executable security/identity/persistence design. Plan lines 208-211 say to use a supported canonical loader/DTO mapper and to specify/approve a compatible typed adapter if needed, but name neither a callable loader nor its contract. The inspected transcript assembly has a canonical YAML writer, while ITranscriptSessionPersister.PersistAsync returns Task<string> (TranscriptContracts.cs:463-476); TranscriptSessionLogPersister maps privately and returns sessionLogId:<id> (lines 30-35). The plan also leaves numeric size limits, invalid-canonical fallback rules, bundle identity/hash validation, and concurrent claim/delete/idempotency mechanism unstated. Repair: pin the actual reusable API or explicitly design the required loader/adapter and compatibility impact; define bounds, allowed roots including ancestor reparse handling, canonical/source identity matching, invalid-versus-missing fallback policy, whole-bundle reconstruction, durable receipt semantics, and atomic claim/compare/delete plus stable replay identity. Add named AC/test cases for those decisions before authorizing this slice. This is not a claim that unrun recovery tests failed.

U2 [P2] Stop reconciliation still delegates its decisive interface and transition rules to implementation. Plan lines 196-198 explicitly defer specifying the reconciliation request/result until the implementer decides whether the current workflow suffices. The safety objective is correct, but the plan does not identify the authoritative query/exact-match extraction, terminal-status rules, or how a completed A response is prevented from overwriting newly active B during the local mutation. Repair: choose the existing client operation or specify the shared operation now; define the identity-bound proof/result shape, pagination/no-match/ambiguous/outage behavior, timestamp/local-state truth table, and identity recheck or conditional mutation before clearing/refreshing the pin. Preserve failed-build/audit enforcement first and do not substitute a different request's completion.

U3 [P2] The provider-aware retry is a goal, not yet an executable algorithm. Plan lines 149 and 213 require three providers, one exact-constraint retry, winner merge, and preservation of unrelated tracked changes, but do not choose the constraint identity/classifier or the failed-save transaction/tracker recovery strategy. The current worktree helper is explicitly SQLite-oriented and uses message substring matching (SessionLogService.cs:680-688), while the retry clears the tracker at line 649. Repair: name the intended unique index/columns and provider-specific structured error/constraint inputs, define which failed entries are detached or rebuilt and how any failed transaction is restored, then specify winner reload/child merge and the single retry boundary. Preserve unrelated pending changes and propagate unrelated uniqueness/cancellation. Tests remain future gates, not current failures.

Plan lines 203 and 209 reuse the existing sourceHash routine and define stable replay identity as workspace + agent + sourceKind + native/root session + sourceHash + ordered native request IDs, then require changed payloads to receive distinct fingerprints. The current routine hashes only the sorted full source-file paths, not file contents (TranscriptRunArtifactWriter.cs:129-134). Changing text or metadata in the same files while retaining native request IDs therefore leaves every listed identity component unchanged. canonicalArtifactSha256 is added to new envelopes at line 203 but is absent from the stated replay-identity formula; normalizedPayloadSha256 is optional. Include it explicitly in the replay key/claim verification and define migration/retention behavior for legacy envelopes without it. State the proof cases: unchanged replay has the same key; changed content at identical paths and request IDs has a different key; canonical and source fallback for equivalent content follow the declared equivalence rule. Do not silently redefine existing SourceHash and invalidate historical envelope identities.

Plan line 219 introduces savepoint creation under 'On the recognized race' and says to establish and roll back a named savepoint before recovering. A savepoint created only after the failed save cannot be the checkpoint for undoing that attempted save. The document must not leave the executor to infer a different temporal sequence, especially after promising exact transaction recovery. Repair: explicitly order snapshot -> establish named savepoint in the active ambient transaction before the first SaveChanges -> attempt save -> classify the failure -> roll back that same pre-existing savepoint -> selectively restore/detach/reload/merge -> one retry. Keep the already-defined no-safe-savepoint/poisoned-context path as classified retryable failure with retained failsafe, and define savepoint release/cleanup without committing or rolling back unrelated caller work.
